key_insight: SkillOpt, an automated prompt-optimization method, dramatically improved cancer-myth false-presupposition correction in LLMs, but the benefit varied by model and sometimes increased over-correction.
clinical_relevance: For cancer communication tools, prompt strategies should be tested on each target model for both false-presupposition correction and preservation of valid clinical assumptions before deployment.
method: Used the physician-verified Cancer-Myth benchmark to train and validate prompt rewrites.
Ran three independent GPT-5.4 SkillOpt optimizations for GPT-4o using FP and NFP examples.
Compared no instruction, strong few-shot prompting, GPT-5.4-generated prompts, and full/compact SkillOpt across seven LLMs.
evidence_signal: On 410 unseen false-presupposition questions, SkillOpt raised GPT-4o correction from 15.4–17.6% to 82.2–90.5%, with strong gains supported by bootstrap confidence intervals and Holm-adjusted p<0.001.
watch_item: SkillOpt was not universally portable and could still challenge valid clinical assumptions, so model-specific validation is essential.
paper_title: Automated Skill Optimisation for False Presupposition Handling in Cancer Communication: SkillOpt Versus Conventional Prompt Engineering Across Language Models
